prerequisites: Minimal familiarity as a common user with computers.

learning_outcomes.text: Locate computer science within engineering disciplines.
Understand the fundamentals of the binary system to comprehend information representation in computers.
Identify the hardware components that constitute a computer system, as well as their interconnection in networks, and understand their basic functioning.
Distinguish the main peripherals used in a computer system and specifically in the field of engineering.
Classify the different types of software used in a computer system.
Identify and classify different types of computer systems and their application domains.
Understand the concept of an algorithm and the process of abstracting a problem in programming.
Identify the program development process and its location within the general Software Engineering process.
Recognize the elementary data structures provided by a structured programming language.
Manage the elementary control structures of a structured programming language.
Abstract operations.
Design small applications to solve elementary problems in collaborative work environments.
Know the main functions performed by an operating system.
Analyze what services the operating system provides to programs and end-users.
Identify the main operating systems used in professional engineering environments and use the main user-level services.
Know the main functions performed by a database management system.
Create data models for simple problems.
Use basic expressions to retrieve and modify information stored in a database.
Identify which database management systems are used in professional engineering environments.
Identify the main application programs used in professional engineering environments.

syllabus_topics: INT - Introduction
Overview of computer science, in the context of other engineering disciplines
Structure and functioning of a computer
Representation of information in a computer
PRO - Introduction to programming
Problem abstraction for programming: fundamental concepts
Variables, expressions, assignment
Use of console input/output
Handling of basic control flow structures: sequential, alternative, and repetitive
Definition and use of subprograms and functions. Variable scope
File input/output
Basic data types and structures
Program development processes. From high level to execution in the processor. Compiled languages and interpreted languages.
BD - Introduction to databases
Concept of database
Fundamentals of the relational data model
Performing queries and modifications
Database Management Systems in professional engineering environments
HSW - Hardware and software components of a computer system
Structure and functioning of a computer: Von Neumann Architecture and machine language
Peripheral devices
System interconnection: types, mechanisms, and applications
Types of software: base software and application software
Types of computer systems and their application domains
SO - Introduction to operating systems
Concept and functions performed by an operating system
Interface and services offered to programs
Interface and services offered to users
Operating systems used in professional engineering environments
Introduction to tools in the practice lab (1h)
Spreadsheet as a tool (3h)
Programming (18h)
Design, implementation, and exploitation of a database (6h)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade consists of 50% theory and 50% practical work. If a score of less than 4 out of 10 is achieved in either part, the final grade will be a fail, calculated as the average of the two parts with a maximum of 4.5 points. To pass, the final grade must be at least 5 out of 10. Unsubmitted evaluable activities count as zero, but if they exceed 50% of the total, the final grade will be 'Not presented'. There are no resit exams for any evaluable parts in the ordinary call. For the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of a theoretical exam (50%) and a practical exam (50%). A minimum score of 5 in both the theoretical and practical exams is required to average the final grade; otherwise, the final grade will be a fail, calculated as the average of the two parts with a maximum of 4.5 points. Students who obtain a grade of 5 or higher in either theory or practical work in a previous call of the current academic year do not have to repeat that part in the second (and last) call. Partial practical grades (Excel, Access, Programming) of 7 or higher are also retained.
